tools.name: resolve_term
tools.description: Where does a word place in the KSA model? The KSA Dictionary is the shared vocabulary that defines the terms a learner uses to assert what they know, do, and are — and the terms a learning offering uses to express what it comprises — so both sides resolve to the same identifiers, never spelling matches. Answers from three linked layers (governed lexicon, O*NET content model, WordNet-derived index), each placement attributed to its layer with provenance; the WordNet placement carries the word's definition (gloss) and synonyms.

term.description: A word for something a person knows or can do, e.g. carpentry or mathematics

tools.name: expand_term
tools.description: What is this word, upward? Walks the WordNet is-a (hypernym) chain meaning to parent meaning, from the word's KSA-mapped sense toward its broader categories, so every step stays in the sense it started in. Each step carries its definition (gloss) and synonyms.

term.description: A word to see what broader kind of thing it is, e.g. carpentry

tools.name: get_dictionary_summary
tools.description: What does the KSA Dictionary hold? The words and meanings it places, the governed terms, the O*NET content-model elements, the link words and the CIP-SOC crosswalk, each with its own version and build date where the layer publishes one, and an honest not held where it does not. Read as published at boot, never computed at request time, and never a word lookup: for one word use resolve_term. The words it holds are those it places; it is not all of WordNet, and the answer says so.

tools.name: look_up_word
tools.description: What does this one word reach? Answers the word as a card: its meanings (each with its definition and part of speech), its family of attested forms and the catalog's own use of it, its KSA placement or its relations, its SOC and CIP codes strongest evidence first (each with every way that reached it and the counts behind it), its O*NET elements by official id, its O*NET Technology Skills, Tools Used and Detailed Work Activity entries under plain labels with O*NET's own names, codes and releases in the detail, its ESCO occupations and skills through the ESCO–O*NET crosswalk, and the next tools by code. Every code carries its official links (O*NET OnLine, BLS, NCES, ESCO). Every call, found or not, returns the step-by-step report of the ten stages it read. Spread is a label, never a penalty. resolve_term is unchanged.

word.description: One word, as written, e.g. negotiate or fundraising

tools.name: words_for_code
tools.description: Which words reach this code? Given an O*NET element id (2.B.1.d), an O*NET-SOC or SOC code (13-1131.00, 13-1131), a CIP code (52.0201), an O*NET Technology Skills (Software Skills) category, a Tools Used UNSPSC commodity code or a Detailed Work Activity id, or an ESCO occupation or skill URI, answers the words that reach it, ranked by the catalog's use of each word under the code; each word's spread is shown as a label, never as a penalty. An ESCO URI is read back through the ESCO–O*NET crosswalk only. Every call, found or not, returns the step-by-step report of the ten stages it read, with the code's official links.

code.description: An O*NET element id, O*NET-SOC or SOC code, CIP code, O*NET layer code, or ESCO URI

tools.name: crosswalk_code
tools.description: What does this code cross to? Auto-detects the family — dotted CIP (52.0201) or dashed SOC (11-1021, O*NET .00 suffix accepted) — and answers the other family's codes and titles from the federal CIP-SOC crosswalk. A program's occupations each carry O*NET's median_annual_wage, demand_signal and bright_outlook where O*NET's cache holds them, null where it holds none.

code.description: A college program code (CIP, e.g. 51.3801) or an occupation code (SOC, e.g. 29-1141)

offset.description: Optional: the next_offset from a previous answer

state.description: Optional two-letter state, e.g. CA: a program's occupations also carry regional_median_annual_wage, the national median times the state's wage ratio, an approximation said so in regional

tools.name: get_occupation
tools.description: What is this occupation? Given a SOC or O*NET-SOC code, answers two records side by side, never merged: O*NET's (its title, every knowledge, skill, ability, work activity and work style item with importance and level, wage, outlook, five related occupations with how many there are, reported job titles, and when it was fetched) and the occupation record (description, typical education, certifications, five related occupations with how many there are, and its programs). A retired SOC follows O*NET's recorded replacement, and the answer says so. An occupation neither record holds is stated, never filled in.

soc.description: An occupation code (SOC, e.g. 29-1141, or O*NET-SOC, e.g. 29-1141.00)

tools.name: open_coach
tools.description: Open a visible coach (coach, advisor, counselor, teacher, mentor or another role) in this chat as an MCP App view, for any service here. Give the role and your service's own context in any shape; send a coach object from an earlier open_coach to reopen the same coach without resetting anything. The view asks the host for fullscreen when the host offers it and shows the mode it actually granted, the coach sized to the space the host gives, and what the host supports. The coach opens as Claude's own picture (the Claude bot) in the internal voice: you speak, in your own voice, as you usually do in this chat, and the person talks to you as they usually do, through this chat's own microphone when they speak; the view makes no sound and its Talk switch is muted. You conduct the conversation: as you speak, send what you are saying to the view with coach_say, in small chunks of about 5 words, so the picture's mouth moves and it blinks with your words. There is nothing to listen for, so end your turn as you usually do; only when the person turns Talk on at the view does it put a line in this chat asking you to listen with coach_listen (a coach session of session_minutes, 30 when omitted). The coaching conversation's words are held only while it is open and are deleted when it closes (24 hours with no activity, or closed); only its id, kind, times and message count are kept. Keep the coach object.

actor.description: Optional: the coach's name; the role when omitted

coach.description: The coaching context an earlier open_coach returned (its coach object). Send it to reopen the same coach: same conversation, same size preset and display mode, nothing reset.

context.description: The calling service's own context for the coach (what is being worked on, where it stands), kept with the coaching context. Sent, it replaces the earlier context; omitted when reopening with coach, the coach keeps the context it had

display_mode.description: The mode the view asks the host for; fullscreen when omitted. The host decides; the view shows what it granted.

role.description: The coach's role, e.g. coach, advisor, counselor, teacher, mentor

script.description: Optional: a GoldCoach script from the store (coach_scripts) for the coach view to load into its script player, in the speaker format: script_id, and stage (get_to_know, navigate or decide; the first when omitted)

session_minutes.description: How long the coach session the person's Talk switch starts lasts, in minutes, when the person names a length; 30 when omitted

size_preset.description: fit: as large as the space allows; natural: the poses' own size, never larger than the space

tools.name: coach_say
tools.description: Send the open coach the words you are saying, so its picture's mouth moves and it blinks with them. In the internal voice (the coach's voice unless the person chose one of the avatar service's on the view) the view makes no sound: you say the words yourself, in your own voice, in this chat, and at the same time send them here in small chunks, about 5 words each, in the order you say them. Chunks sent while the picture is still moving wait their turn. Optional cues (the avatar service's show_frame, action, head, set_caption, speaking, mouth_shapes, blink, idle, auto_revert) go at sentence or beat boundaries. While a service is being called, keep talking with the person about the process and about how their answers are affirming, in a motivational voice, and send those words too. The view shows the words beside the picture as it moves through them. speaker is claude when omitted: the view shows Claude's own picture (the Claude bot); speaker avatar shows the coach's own picture (the avatar service's avatar) for those words. Where the person chose one of the avatar service's voices on the view, the view sounds the words it is sent in that voice. view switches the picture now (claude, avatar, or camera: the person's own camera, which their browser asks them to allow); whoever speaks next takes it back. Use the coach_id open_coach returned. The answer says what was queued; a queued chunk is not evidence the person saw it.

arguments.description: The cue's own arguments, as the avatar service's tool of that name takes them

reply_to.description: Optional: the message this answers, when it came through the coach

speaker.description: Who says it: claude (you, in Claude's own picture; the default) or avatar (the coach's own picture shows for the words)

text.description: The words you are saying now: a small chunk of your sentence, about 5 words

view.description: Optional: the picture to show now: avatar, claude (the Claude bot) or camera (the person's own camera)

tools.name: coach_listen
tools.description: Listen for the person's next spoken reply to the open coach: only when the person has turned Talk on at the coach view. The coach opens with Talk muted; the person then talks to you through this chat as usual and there is nothing to listen for, so do not call this. When they turn Talk on, the view starts a coach session and puts a line in this chat asking you to listen, with the coach_id, the seat and the session_ends_at to listen with: call this at once when that line comes. While Talk is on, each time they pause at the end of a thought the view sends what they said to the coach, not into this chat; when a reply goes unheard, the view puts the line in this chat again. This waits up to wait_seconds for it and answers what they said (status heard, with the message number), that they said nothing yet (status silent), that they have said nothing for 8 seconds since the coach finished speaking (status quiet: ask them once, through the coach, whether they are still there, as one short question with nothing said after it, then keep listening quietly), or that the session's time is up (status session_over: say goodbye through the coach, tell them they can turn Talk on to start another session, and end your turn). When the person plays a script on the coach view it also answers that the script is playing, with the script (status script: follow its order), that the person said their own line in it (status heard_in_script: do not answer then), that your own line has come (status your_line: say it at once with coach_say, speaker claude), or that the script is done (status script_done). When it hears them: at once, in the same step, call coach_say with an acknowledgment spoken with the nod: thank them, say aloud that you understood, and say what you are about to do, then, while the service runs, chat with them about the process and about how their answers are affirming, in a motivational voice (reply_to set to the message number, with a head nod cue), and call the service the request needs; when the service answers, call coach_say with the answer and coach_board with its key points or a picture when they help; then call coach_listen again, in the same turn; when it answers silent or quiet, call it again; do not end your turn before the session's time is up or they say they are done. Use the coach_id, the seat and the session_ends_at the view's line gives.

session_ends_at.description: When the coach session ends: the session_ends_at in the line the coach view put in the chat, as given

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the person to speak (the most when omitted; 0 only looks)

tools.name: coach_board
tools.description: Show the whiteboard beside the open coach, or close it (show false). It shows a title, an answer's text and a picture: image_url is an https picture on the web, which is fetched for the view (the view may not load other sites' pictures; at most 1 MB). While it is shown, the coach view splits its space between the coach and the whiteboard. Use it when the person asks to see something (a campus, a chart, an answer written out) or asks for the whiteboard, and with an answer whose key points or picture help the person follow what the coach says; close it when they are done. Use the coach_id open_coach returned. The answer says what was queued; queued is not evidence the person saw it.

caption.description: Optional: where the picture is from; its site when omitted

image_url.description: Optional: an https address of a picture to show

show.description: true shows the whiteboard with what is given; false closes it

text.description: Optional: the answer or notes to show

tools.name: coach_scripts
tools.description: The GoldCoach scripts held (the latest version of each): their labels, their tags (life stage, situation, goal), their phases (as many as each script needs), the CourseShelf areas they rely on, and the trial (the opening script plus one avenue). The opening script, Getting to know each other, always runs first; after it, offer the scripts whose tags fit where the person is and where they want to go, and let the person choose. Send tags to list only the ones that fit.

tags.description: Optional: words to fit, by dimension

tools.name: coach_script
tools.description: Step through a GoldCoach script. Without at: the entry of a stage (the first when stage is omitted). With at (the message you just asked) and the person's response (affirmed, corrected or rejected for a statement; yes or no; answered for a free answer): the message that follows from what they said, so two people starting the same script get different routes, each traceable to their own statements (send the statement_ids the response followed). Each step names the GoldSeam tools to call in order and the CourseShelf areas it relies on. With the session open_my_coach returned (session_id and person_handle), each step is recorded on the person's record (the script run, the stage reached, where to continue) and a milestone the step carries is recorded, not shared with the sponsor until the person shares it (coach_milestone_share). The check-in script answers the person's record first. In a trial sponsorship only the opening script and the first avenue answer. With email_my_history true, the session and the address the person typed: their GoldCoach history (sessions, scripts, stages, milestones; never the words) is emailed to them.

routed_from.description: With start_at: the script whose bridge handed over

tools.name: playlist_summary
tools.description: How often have playlists been explored? Counts from the playlist store: policies and playlists by status, explorations with hits and first runs, the most-explored playlists, one playlist's line tallies, reviews and run shares. Small counts are shown as fewer than 5. Explorations are runs, not people. Also, by built_by, for policies and for playlists: saves, first-try passes, average attempts to pass, and reviews that confirmed or rejected; and for playlists, candidates on their own line, not among saves: build, the builds kept beside a trusted playlist, and verification, the verifier's kept rebuilds. verifier gives the independent verifier's models, its nightly cap, what its latest night did for playlists and for school policies and, where it verifies nothing, why. audit gives, for each verifier, how often a review confirmed its ai_verified playlists correct or found them wrong, and the accuracy rate.

checklist_id.description: Optional: one checklist, by its checklist_id from an earlier answer; adds that checklist's playlist lines with their tallies

since.description: Optional: count only what was recorded on or after this UTC date, YYYY-MM-DD

unitid.description: Optional: one school, by its IPEDS UNITID

tools.name: playlist_policy_open
tools.description: Start or reuse one school's policy: its institution-wide rules, worked out once and used by every playlist at that school. Pages are read from captured HTML or from an anchored PDF page range: a PDF page is named page:<file>#page=N-N, its running headers, footers and page numbers removed, and no links are gathered from it. Finds the school's captured pages that carry institution-wide rules, then answers hit (the stored policy, its policy_id, status and trust_state), or stale or miss with a manifest of sections to read with playlist_read: award_types, policies, one page:<capture_file> for each qualifying page, and designations, each with its character count. On stale it also returns the stored policy, so you can see what changed. The server calls no AI model: you read the sections, reason over them yourself, and send the policy with playlist_policy_save. On stale or miss the answer also carries procedure, a numbered list of steps that is the same for every caller, and procedure_version: follow the steps in their order; area_lines, the area names the school's checklists use, each a query for playlist_find_pages; and award_titles, the award titles the school's programs use: a policy gives an award rule for each award title and a designation for each area line where the school's pages state one. Pass rebuild true to build a held policy again: a hit then carries the sections, the next step and the procedure as well, and the policy in use is replaced only when a new one passes its save. The qualifying pages begin with the pages the school's academic policy index points at, the closest to the content first, at most 4. Where the school's academic policy index is held, the answer also carries policy_index: the school's index rows (kind, scope, award_title, area_name, department, program_id, title, capture_file, source_url, quote, rank), and with checklist_id the rows scoped to that checklist's program and to its college or department. No row is a ruling: a quote is evidence you cite exactly as printed, read from its page.

checklist_id.description: Optional: a checklist at this school; the policy index rows scoped to its program and to its college or department are listed beside the school's

rebuild.description: Optional: true to get the sections to read though a policy is held, so the policy can be built again

unitid.description: The school, by its IPEDS UNITID

tools.name: playlist_read
tools.description: Read one section named in a manifest, in full: give unitid for a section of a school's policy (from playlist_policy_open), or checklist_id for a section of a checklist's playlist (from playlist_open). A section over 60,000 characters is returned in parts: the answer carries part and next_part, and you ask again with part set to next_part until next_part is null. Pages come in cleaned text, the same text every source quote is checked against. With unitid, section page:<capture_file> reads any capture held for the school, such as one playlist_find_pages found, not only the pages the manifest lists. Read-only.

checklist_id.description: The checklist whose playlist section to read; give this or unitid, not both

part.description: Optional: which part of a long section, from 1 (default 1)

section.description: The section's name exactly as the manifest gives it

unitid.description: The school whose policy section to read; give this or checklist_id, not both

tools.name: playlist_find_pages
tools.description: Search every capture held for one school, across all of its catalog folders, not only the pages playlist_policy_open selected. Use it when a designation, award rule or note is not in the manifest's sections. Give unitid and query: plain words, or a code such as SI. Words are matched as one phrase, without regard to case; a query of 2 to 4 capital letters is matched as a whole token in its own case, so SI does not match SIGN or basic. Returns up to 25 matches: the pages whose source_url the school's academic policy index holds first (in_policy_index true), then the pages with the most hits. Each match gives the capture_file exactly as playlist_read and the save checks name it, its source_url, its character count, how many hits the page holds, and a snippet of about 200 characters around each hit, up to 5 a page. The text searched is the same cleaned text every source quote is checked against, so what you find can be quoted verbatim: read the page with playlist_read (unitid, and section page:<capture_file>). Read-only.

unitid.description: The school, by its IPEDS UNITID

tools.name: playlist_policy_diagnose
tools.description: Diagnose one school's policy: what stands between the school and a policy, read and nothing else. No model is called, nothing is saved and nothing in the store is changed. Give unitid. The answer gives walks, the school's catalog captures with what Gather coded as policy in each; pages_the_open_would_read, the pages playlist_policy_open would read now, how many the folder list picks and whether the courseleaf stopgap stood in for it; gather_policy_coded and harvest_policy_records_name, each page Gather coded as policy and each file Harvest's policy records name, marked chosen or left out with the reason (not on the list, an excluded segment, not HTML, an older copy of the address, not held); policies_held, every policy row held for the school with its status, trust_state, built_by, created_at, its pages and the pages it lacks against what would be read now, and which one is in use; open_would_answer, the outcome playlist_policy_open would give now (hit, stale, miss or no_pages) and why; award_titles, each award title with its programs' published credits, whether the policy in use has a rule for it, and what the server could infer for its minimum credits; and area_lines, each area line with the number of captured pages that print it. Read-only.

unitid.description: The school, by its IPEDS UNITID

tools.name: playlist_policy_standing
tools.description: One school's policy as the Playlist Builds list shows it, read and nothing else. No model is called and nothing is saved. Give unitid. The answer gives policy_in_use, the policy an open or a run would use (policy_id, source: pages, inferred or survey, source_by, trust_state, status, built_by, created_at, capture_year), or null where none is in use; and missing_content, each kind in its own field: no_policy_pages, true where none of the school's captured pages carries institution-wide rules, and pages_policy_lacks, the pages the open would read now that are not among the pages the policy in use was saved with (capture_file, source_url); and walk, the walk an operator's Surf asked Gather for, as its file holds it (standing asked, walking, filed or not_filed, with the file's own words), or null where none was asked. For the full account of a school's pages and policies use playlist_policy_diagnose. Read-only.

unitid.description: The school, by its IPEDS UNITID

tools.name: playlist_policy_surf
tools.description: Surf: ask Gather for a walk of one school's catalog pages, or read where that walk stands. Give unitid; give ask true to record the ask, and leave it out to only read. This tool starts no walk and no run. The ask is one file the box writes, standing asked. Gather's own window on the box PC, when it is open and no run is going, takes the oldest ask, walks the school's catalog in the window, and rewrites the file: walking, then filed (capture, pages_kept, policy_pages_kept) or not_filed, each with words in Gather's own words. Where a walk for the school already stands at asked or walking, no second one is asked for. The answer gives asked, true when this call recorded an ask, and walk, the ask as its file holds it, or null where none was asked. Once a walk is filed, the school's policy pages are chosen from its pages too, so a Rebuild reads them.

ask.description: True to record the ask; left out, the call only reads where the walk stands

unitid.description: The school, by its IPEDS UNITID

tools.name: playlist_policy_infer
tools.description: Save a basic policy for one school from the server's own inference, with no AI. Give unitid. It saves one award rule for each award title the server can infer a minimum for (from the school's programs' published credits, or else from the award's level: 60 for an associate degree, 120 for a bachelor's degree), each with inferred_min_credits and inferred_basis and no quote, and no designations. The policy's source is inferred, its trust state unverified, and its built_by names inference. It never replaces a policy in use that was built from the school's own pages: it then refuses, says so, and points to a rebuild. Where no award title has an inference it says so and saves nothing. The answer gives the saved policy, its policy_id, status, trust_state and source, and awards: each award title with its programs, their published credits, and what was inferred.

unitid.description: The school, by its IPEDS UNITID

tools.name: playlist_policy_survey
tools.description: Save a policy for one school from a person's answers. Give unitid, name (the person who answered) and policy: award_rules, each an award_title with its min_credits and other conditions; designations, each a designation with its credits and the course codes that carry it; and notes. No quote is asked for or checked. Each award title must be one of the school's, each minimum a positive number (or left out where the server can infer one), and each course code one of the school's learning units; answers that fail a check come back with each error and nothing is saved. The policy's source is survey, with the person's name, its built_by is survey: <name>, and its trust state is unverified. It never replaces a policy in use that was built from the school's own pages: it then refuses, says so, and points to a rebuild.

name.description: The name of the person whose answers these are

policy.description: award_rules: [{ award_title, min_credits, other }]; designations: [{ designation, credits, courses }]; notes: [text]

unitid.description: The school, by its IPEDS UNITID

tools.name: playlist_policy_save
tools.description: Save one school's policy after the server checks it. Every source is a capture_file held for the school, one playlist_policy_open named or one playlist_find_pages found (the cabinet path, without the page: its section name carries), and a quote of 300 characters or fewer copied verbatim from that capture's cleaned text; the quote check is exact, with no fuzzy matching. The server also checks that every course code is one of the learning units in the school's catalog, every award_title appears in the award_types section, and every min_credits is a positive number. Where a policy built from the school's pages is in use, every designation and award rule it holds must be kept, by its name or award_title, unless its own page no longer shows it (its source quote is no longer in that capture); a policy that drops one its page still shows is refused. A designation's quote must contain its name or its abbreviation, and every course in its courses list must be supported, in one of two ways. One: its code and the designation's abbreviation or name appear together in one quote, the source's or one in the designation's optional evidence list. A row counts where it sits under that heading and before the next heading, and one evidence quote may show several rows. Where a school defines a designation by subject and level instead of a list of courses, give subjects: each rule is a subject prefix, an optional minimum course number, and its own source, whose quote shows them. It never alters the policy. It returns policy_id, status, and every error in plain words: a policy with errors is saved as rejected, so correct it and save again.

tools.name: playlist_open
tools.description: Start or reuse one checklist's playlist: its requirements, with its school's policy, set out as an ordered sequence of lines. A checklist is read from its captured HTML page or from an anchored PDF page range: for a PDF capture the requirements section gives source_kind pdf, the pages read and the checklist's stored requirement lines beside the text, requirements_html is null, no linked pages are gathered (links_statement says so), and capture_file names the PDF with the pages read (<file>#page=N-M). It needs a saved school policy and names playlist_policy_open as the next call when there is none. Answers hit (the stored playlist, its playlist_id and status), or stale or miss with a manifest of sections to read with playlist_read: stored_rows, requirements, requirements_html, courses, one linked:<capture_file> for each page the requirement section links to that the cabinet holds, and policy. Links the cabinet does not hold are listed by URL. On stale it also returns the stored playlist. You read the sections, reason over them yourself, and send the lines with playlist_save. On stale or miss the answer also carries procedure, a numbered list of steps that is the same for every caller, and procedure_version: follow the steps in their order; and area_lines, the area names the school's checklists use, each a query for playlist_find_pages. A stored playlist that was built under a school policy that is no longer the one in use is out of date: the answer is stale, with policy_rebuilt true and the sections to rebuild it, and a new build that passes takes its place whatever its trust. Where the checklist's only playlist was rejected, the answer is a miss that says so: rejected is playlist, and trust has state rejected with its sentence. Every answer carries verified: true only when a run of the stored playlist would be verified, that is when the playlist's trust state and its school policy's are both ai_verified or school_confirmed; false where no playlist is held. Read verified; do not work it out from the state. Every answer carries trust: the playlist's trust state, who built it and when, who verified or confirmed it and when, its catalog edition, the school policy's state, and one sentence. Always tell the person the trust statement. A playlist's status (draft, rejected or superseded) is its save lifecycle only; its trust_state is how far it can be trusted: published_only, unverified, ai_verified, school_confirmed, needs_rereview or rejected. mapped_from says what the answer is from: playlist, with its playlist_id and trust state, or harvested_checklist.

checklist_id.description: The checklist, by its checklist_id from an earlier answer

rebuild.description: Optional: true to get the sections to read though a playlist is held, so the playlist can be built again; a held playlist is then answered stale, and stays in use until a new one passes its save

tools.name: playlist_save
tools.description: Save one checklist's playlist after the server checks it. lines is the ordered list of the playlist's lines. The server checks that line_ids are unique and order runs 1, 2, 3 without gaps; that the credits of every line except option_list and note add up to the published credits (within the range, where a range is published); that every slot's fills_from names an option_list and every option_list is named by a slot; that every course code is one of the school's learning units; that every area designation is in the school policy; that choose has n no greater than its courses; that every quote appears verbatim in the capture its source names, which may be the requirements section, a linked section, or any other capture held for the checklist's school; and that every course code of the checklist's requirement items that the school holds appears in a line or in a note line that names it (a footnote, a permission note or a tag in parentheses outside the items is not counted); and that every checklist item naming a learning unit with published credits is on a course, one_of, choose or option_list line or accepted by an area line, never only a note; that the playlist carries the last requirement group the checklist holds (a playlist that ends before it is never saved); that options the page prints as a choice or as "or" alternatives are not each a required course line, and no course is on two course lines; that every course code a line carries is printed in the requirements, on a linked page or in the line's quote; that a note line carries no course codes; and that a restricted line carries its rule. Where the credits do not add up, the error names the lines that carry no requirement item, or the groups printed with credits that no line carries. It never alters what the lines say; it adds accepts to each area line and min_courses where the text names a number of courses. It returns playlist_id, status, and every error in plain words, each naming its line: lines with errors are saved as rejected, so correct them and save again. A build that passes replaces the playlist in use only when there is none, when the catalog page has changed, or when the one in use is unverified or rejected. Otherwise it is kept as a candidate: the answer gives candidate_id and the playlist in use, the candidate is never used for anyone's progress, and playlist_compare compares the two.

accept_warnings.description: Optional, false where left out: true saves the result with its warnings. A value's shape, a line's kind and its line_id still refuse the save, and so do a playlist that ends before the last requirement group, options made each a required line or a course on two course lines, a quote not found verbatim or a capture not held, a course code on a note line, and a code the page does not print. A quote over 300 characters is cut at a word boundary with "…" (marked quote trimmed); every other check marks what it concerns not established. Each mark is kept in that item's warnings, and the result is saved with trust state partial, or inferred where it rests on an inferred policy.

dropped.description: Checklist rows the playlist leaves out, each {table, row_id, why}: page furniture such as a planner, a year heading or a bare "and". A course the page requires is never dropped; a group is dropped only once nothing sits under it.

row_id.description: The row's id as stored_rows.shape gives it: a group's group_id, an item's item_id, a note's position

flagged.description: Values the page does not support, left blank, or printed but not reading as a requirement, kept as printed: each {table, row_id, field, why}. Never worked out by adding or subtracting.

groups.description: The playlist in the checklist's shape: the checklist's groups, as stored_rows.shape holds them, each with group_id. A group the checklist holds is copied as it is except for the fields given; each given field that differs from the checklist needs the page's words in fills (fills.<field>: a quote from the checklist's own capture, or {capture_file, quote}). A group the checklist lacks (an id starting PG_) is added, with its quote in fills.row. items: the group's items, the same way (item_id; an item set under another group is moved); an item's alternatives and nodes, where given, are that item's whole list. nodes: the group's rules, its whole list: each a requirement node with requirement_kind (one of: consent, placement, level, exclusion, elective, open_elective, gpa, total, cap, min_grade, repeat_limit, overlap, residency, honor, substitution, exception), measure_quantity, measure_unit, measure_comparator (at_least or at_most), measure_scope, condition_text, and printed_text, the page's own words. A group is never its own ancestor, and chooses no more than the items and groups under it.

fills.description: The page's words for each field given that differs from the checklist, keyed by that field's name (for example credits_published, parent_group_id, required_choice_count), and row for a row the checklist lacks: each value a quote from the checklist's own capture as a string, or {capture_file, quote}. An object, never a list.

The page's words for each field given that differs from the checklist, keyed by that field's name (for example credits_published, parent_group_id, required_choice_count), and row for a row the checklist lacks: each value a quote from the checklist's own capture as a string, or {capture_file, quote}. An object, never a list.

notes.description: The checklist's notes the playlist changes or adds: position, note_text, note_mark, fills, and nodes (the rules the note prints, as for a group). A note the checklist holds is named by its position. A note the checklist lacks is added with its quote in fills.row; left without a position, it takes the next one.

fills.description: The page's words for each field given that differs from the checklist, keyed by that field's name (for example credits_published, parent_group_id, required_choice_count), and row for a row the checklist lacks: each value a quote from the checklist's own capture as a string, or {capture_file, quote}. An object, never a list.

built_by.description: Who built this playlist: a short string naming the agent and model. Stored with the saved playlist. A save without it is rejected.

courses.description: Course codes, for course, one_of, choose and option_list; otherwise empty

credits.description: A number; null only for option_list and note

designation.description: area only: the designation exactly as in the school policy. The save stores on the line, as accepts, the course list the policy holds for the designation; only those courses, or a course of a subject the policy defines the designation by, fill it

fills_from.description: slot only: the line_id of an option_list

heading.description: The group heading the line sits under on the page, as printed

kind.description: course: one required course. one_of: one course from a short list printed on the line. choose: n courses or credits from courses printed together; a list the page says to choose from ("Select two of the following") is one choose line, never each option a course line. slot: filled from an option list elsewhere on the page. option_list: a list that feeds slots and never adds to the total by itself. area: any course carrying a designation from the school policy. open: any course that earns credit. note: a printed condition that is not itself credit; it carries no course codes. restricted: a named elective the page restricts by a printed rule, such as "Business Elective" or "Major Elective Course numbered 2000-3999"; it carries credits and the rule as printed in rule, and no course codes. A checklist item that names a learning unit and carries published credits is never a note: it is a course or one_of line, and a printed condition on it (such as being waived by another course) is a note beside it.

major_elective.description: true on the program's major elective line: it is filled after the area lines and before the open electives

min_courses.description: area, slot and open only: the number of courses the line asks for, where it asks for courses rather than credits. Where it is not given, the save stores it from the line's text when the text names courses, no credits, and one number

rule.description: restricted only: the elective's rule as the page prints it, such as "Major Elective Course numbered 2000-3999"

source.description: Where the school published it: the capture, named as the manifest or playlist_find_pages names it, and a verbatim passage of 300 characters or fewer from that capture's cleaned text

text.description: One plain sentence a person could follow
examples: Take one BUS/DPR elective from the list below.

waived_by.description: Optional, on a line that carries credit: the condition the page prints under which the line is not required, such as a course passed at a minimum grade. A run marks the line met by waiver, with 0 credits, when a held course that lands as one of these courses meets min_grade; the waiving course is shown apart and still fills its own line. Where the held grade is not a letter grade (a P, a score), the line is uncertain, reason "waiver grade not a letter grade", naming the course and grade; where no grade is held for it, reason "waiver grade not held", named the same way.

courses.description: The course codes that waive the line, each one of the school's learning units

min_grade.description: The lowest letter grade the page prints for the waiver, exactly as printed (such as C-); null where it prints none. Where given, the source quote shows it.

tools.name: playlist_run
tools.description: Play a person's held courses through a checklist's stored playlist and get their progress line by line. Checklists are read from captured HTML or from an anchored PDF page range. Give checklist_id and held, the whole list each time. Every held course is landed in one call: a course taken at the playlist's school lands as itself, a course from another school lands as the receiving course the school's known transfer rules name, a course with no known mapping is unresolved, and a failing or withdrawn grade (F, U, NC, NP, W) does not land. An answer that is not done carries continue: send continue back unchanged, with the same checklist_id and held, until the answer says done. Each line takes landed courses until its target (its courses or credits) is reached, in this order: course and one_of lines, choose lines, slot and area lines, the major elective, then open electives. The last call's answer gives the summary, every line with its state (met, partial, open, uncertain or not_a_course), its target, what was assigned and every held course placed on it, credit_short where a course meets a line on its code with fewer credits, the credits applied (each placed course once, by what it landed as), the step timings and the steps (the rule lookup, landing and settlement, each with its outcome, count and ms), what the person still needs, what did not count and why, the playlist's id, status and source, and a run_token. If no active, validated playlist is held for the checklist, the answer says so and names playlist_open as the next call; a run is never made against the harvested checklist. If the playlist, or the school policy it rests on, is rejected, nothing is run either: the answer says which of the two was rejected and names the call that rebuilds it. Pass first_run true when the playlist was assembled in this same conversation, immediately before the run. The person's courses are never stored: they come in each call and go back in continue, which you keep. Only the run's line states, counts and timings are recorded, after the answer. Every answer carries trust: the run's trust state, the weaker of the playlist's and its school policy's, with who built the playlist and when, who verified or confirmed it and when, its catalog edition, and one sentence. Always tell the person the trust statement. A run whose trust state is below ai_verified says Unverified. mapped_from says what the answer is from: playlist, with its playlist_id and trust state, or harvested_checklist where no playlist is held and nothing was run.

checklist_id.description: The checklist, by its checklist_id from an earlier answer

continue.description: From the previous answer: its continue, sent back unchanged. Leave it out on the first call

first_run.description: First call only: true when the playlist was assembled in this same conversation, immediately before the run; otherwise the run is recorded as a hit

held.description: The courses the person holds, as many as there are, the whole list on every call, in the form checklist_map accepts: each { unitid or school, code, title, credits, grade, term }. An empty list runs the checklist with no courses or exams: one call, every line that asks for a course is open, and the answer says what is still needed

A run that is not verified, because the trust state of its playlist or of its school's policy is below ai_verified, is shared with the Unverified label: the answer says so, and so does the share link each time it is opened.

tools.name: playlist_review
tools.description: Record a review of one saved playlist or one saved school policy. Give playlist_id or policy_id, one and not both, with reviewer (a name), reviewer_type (human, school or ai_verifier) and decision (confirm or reject). note is optional. The review sets the row's trust_state and never its status: a school's confirm sets school_confirmed; a human's or an AI verifier's confirm sets ai_verified and records the reviewer in verified_by; a reject sets rejected. A confirm of a playlist that was already ai_verified counts as a correct result in the weekly audit, and a human's reject of one as a wrong result. A reviewer may not confirm a row it built (its built_by). A run drops the Unverified label only when its playlist and its school policy are both ai_verified or school_confirmed. tools.name: playlist_compare
tools.description: Compare a candidate playlist with a golden checklist's golden playlist, line by line. The golden set is a small list of checklists. A checklist in it gets its golden playlist, its reference, only when a person confirms one through playlist_review with reviewer_type human; until then the answer says no golden playlist is held for the checklist yet, and nothing is compared. Give checklist_id, one in the golden set, and playlist_id, the candidate: a playlist of the same checklist, as playlist_save returned it. For each line of the golden playlist the answer says whether the candidate has a line that matches it in kind, credits and courses, or how the candidate's line differs, or that the candidate has none; and it lists the candidate's lines the golden playlist does not have. Give against_playlist_id as well to compare the candidate with that saved playlist of the same checklist instead, on kind, credits, courses, designation and fills_from; the checklist then need not be in the golden set, and agrees says whether every line does. checklist_id.description: A checklist in the golden set

playlist_id.description: The candidate playlist's playlist_id, or the candidate_id of a build that playlist_save kept as a candidate

tools.name: playlist_review_queue

For each one waiting the answer gives playlist_id and checklist_id, or for a school policy its policy_id, with school, built_by, verified_by and picked_at, when it was picked. tools.name: enrichment_run
tools.description: Enrichment orders on the work-order queue, run by the box. action start, with area (one of the Index's key ids, e.g. credit-by-exam), schools (a list, each a UNITID or a school's name; a name is taken only when it matches one school) and dry_run (default false), writes the order WO-V<MMDD>-<NN>_ENRICHMENT.md to the work-orders folder and runs it in the background, one order at a time. For each school on its own it runs, in order: discover and rekey (the Index's keys for the area's pages; rekey backs up institutions.json), Gather with --recapture-what-we-hold, Harvest, the area's check and post, and the Serve load for the school and area. A step that fails ends that school; the others still run. A dry run writes nothing but the steps' records: rekey and check without apply, Gather and Harvest skipped, Serve's plan only. action status, with number, answers the order's state, each school's steps, the report and, once it ends, the Normandy notice, ready to send (nothing is published or sent). action list (the default) answers the enrichment orders, newest first, and the areas the phrase table holds. Example: 'enrich Temple and Arizona, credit by exam' is start with schools ["Temple University", "University of Arizona"] and area credit-by-exam.

tools.name: playlist_rebuild_orders
tools.description: The rebuild orders the playlist store writes for the Queue's build job. An order is written the moment a school's policy or a checklist's playlist is found stale (its pages or its catalog page differ from what is read now), when a stored playlist fails the current save check, and, when a school's policy passes its save and replaces the one in use, for every playlist built on the replaced policy. At most one order is open or taken per policy or playlist, and an order that ended done or dropped is not written again for the same row and reason. action list (the default) answers the orders, the oldest first, with an optional status (open, taken, done or dropped) and limit (default 50, at most 500). action take, with order_id, makes one open order taken; a playlist order waits, answered taken false with the reason, while its school's policy order is open or taken. action finish, with order_id and ending (done or dropped), ends a taken order, with the optional request_id that ran it and a note of what the build said. action release, with order_id and note, turns a taken order whose build was lost back to open, keeping the note in result_note; it is not ended, so it counts as neither done nor dropped. The row in use keeps serving until a rebuild passes its save and replaces it.

Answered only to main KSAserver's own key: the requests hold the emails of learners who asked for their result by email; any other caller is refused. action list (the default) answers the requests, the newest first, with an optional limit. action get, with request_id, answers one. action open, with request (the request to write) and open_statuses, writes it unless a request for the same key (a policy rebuild: its school; a checklist build: its checklist) has one of those statuses, in which case the optional learner joins that request; started says which. action requeue, with request_id, open_statuses and set, sets those fields on the request unless another request for the same key has one of those statuses; queued says which, with the reason. action set, with request_id and set, sets those fields. action carry_over, with source and requests, carries main's old request file over once; without requests it answers whether the carry-over was made.

tools.name: playlist_schools
tools.description: One row for each school the playlist store holds a policy, an index run, a playlist or a build request for, ordered by state, then school name. tools.name: checklist_map
tools.description: How far along am I in a program at a school I am considering? One checklist at any target school, chosen by its name or title (or its checklist_id), line by line against what a person holds. Each held item is compared through the combined check. Two equal sources, four steps run side by side: (1) comparability direct from the catalogs - the receiver's own published mappings; (2) known equivalencies direct from CourseAtlas, live - what institutions report, CollegeBoard's among them as CourseAtlas carries them; (3) inferred comparability from the catalogs' comparability anchors (hop 1: an exam at a shared score, a state course, a mapping, crossing kinds); (4) inferred equivalency from CourseAtlas's equivalency anchors (hop 2, its own chain). Step 4, CourseAtlas inferred, runs only when sources asks for it. `kind` narrows them: known runs 1 and 2, inferred runs 3 and 4, both runs all four. Each landing is joined to the checklist's lines; the person's package, when given, adds the lines its prior learning may meet. Each line is met (a known mapping lands a held item on it), reached_by_inference (only an inferred landing reaches it: shown with its path of published links, never counted as met), may_be_met_by_prior_learning, or open, with every way it is reached. Each group gives its lines by state beside the choice rule it prints. Last, what does not count: each held item that reaches no line, with its reason (no rule, below the score, landing on a course this checklist does not require, unresolved, not held, or a source not read - never an absence). A case to show the school, not a verdict; recognition is the school's act. The answer says what it was mapped_from. Where the checklist has a playlist, the held items are mapped through the playlist's lines, settled as playlist_run settles them: mapped_from is playlist, with playlist_id and the trust block; lines and groups are the playlist's lines under its printed headings, each met, open, uncertain or not_a_course; credits gives the credits applied, and program_progress gives credits remaining and percent complete only where the catalog prints one credit total; nothing is recorded as a run. Where the checklist has no playlist yet, mapped_from is harvested_checklist, the answer carries trust with state published_only and names playlist_open as the next call. Where the checklist's only playlist was rejected, the answer says so: rejected is playlist, trust has state rejected with its sentence, playlist_open is named as the call that rebuilds it, and the map still shows the school's requirements as published. In the harvested map, a held course that fits several groups that print no choice rule is counted as met in none of them and is listed once under overlapping_group_choices. Always tell the person the trust statement. Each row names its current FORM's wording source: source_url, capture_file, catalog_year and source_catalog_name are that one source's, never the record's whole span. A row whose record holds more than one form or more than one source also carries version_count, source_count, first_edition_seen and last_edition_seen, and one sentence saying so in words; a record with one form and one source carries none of them and reads exactly as it always has. The forms themselves, each with its own content and its own sources, come from the one-record get, never from a list.

A rule with several receiving courses takes the class of its least held one. For each likely_renumbered rule, the checklists that require the named course are counted. The answer: a summary of counts per class, then one row per rule outside held_current and generic_credit, sorted by checklists affected, highest first, each with its CourseAtlas source_url, and every read as a step with its count and ms. A call reads until its time is spent and answers with `continue.arguments` to send back as they are; the counts carry across calls, the rows are each call's own. Read-only: it changes no rule, playlist or catalog row. Recognition is the school's act; findings are for the school to confirm. Each row names its current FORM's wording source: source_url, capture_file, catalog_year and source_catalog_name are that one source's, never the record's whole span. tools.description: The person's Selfie from their evidence package, read from their own words through the KSA Dictionary by pattern matching, with no AI: the same package gives the same Selfie. Each item quotes the words it was read from, or names the course row or life experience, names the document and the Dictionary entry that placed it, and carries one of five governed bands (emerging signal, plausible, supported, strongly supported, corroborated candidate) with the basis that put it there; its level (Bloom, Dreyfus or O*NET Level) is a separate field. A transcript's courses are read as their held learning units. Program (CIP) and occupation (SOC) codes are reached by crossing, each with its chain; O*NET's elements for those occupations come as candidates with O*NET's published Importance and Level, never as shown. With the Selfie come an affirmation for each dimension the evidence supports and a first-person positional statement (with the aspiration, when given), naming only the person's own items and documents and saying "may". It mirrors, for the person to confirm, refine or reject; it is never a grade or a credit decision. The person's placements and dismissals in the package's selfie.learner_decisions are honored. tools.name: draft_my_claims
tools.description: Make the credit claims a person's learning supports, from their package. The answer names its path in `path`. The Selfie interview path (`goldseam`): when the package holds a Selfie interview (make_my_selfie, add_to_my_selfie, respond_to_my_statements) with at least one statement the person affirmed, even beside a document Selfie, each affirmed statement is one claim in the person's own words, with the words it came from and its KSA Dictionary identifiers. Nothing is drafted, no AI is called and no confidence number is assigned; a statement they reject or remove in their Selfie is no longer a claim. The agent path (`agent`): through GoldSeam no AI is called here, so for a package holding only a document Selfie (after my_selfie_ksa_view) you, the person's agent, draft the claims: without `claims` the answer's for_your_agent holds the drafting instructions and the evidence to draft from; draft them in the person's chat, show them, and call again with the same package and `claims`. The OpenAI path (`openai`) is AcademyOne's own GoldRibbon app's, where AcademyOne's AI drafts them. Either way each claim quotes the document it rests on. They are drafts for the person to keep, affirm or decline (set each claim's confidence to ratified, affirmed or declined in the package); the AI never affirms a claim. Give the school they are thinking of as `school` so its catalog is made ready for suggest_credit_for_my_learning. Nothing is stored: the answer returns the package for the agent to keep.

tools.name: suggest_credit_for_my_learning
tools.description: Where is a person in the program they are aiming for, and what may their learning meet? Name the program with `checklist_id` (find it with find_programs at that school) and the answer is that program's checklist line by line: the lines their claims may meet, each with the claim, how well it is corroborated and every link cited; the lines a transfer answer in their package already covers; and the lines still needed. Learning no line matches stands as block credit. Without a program, no course is suggested and the claims stand as block credit. The answer names its path in `path`. On the Selfie interview path (`goldseam`: the package holds a Selfie interview statement the person affirmed), no AI is called: each claim's candidate courses are ranked by the KSA Dictionary (the identifiers the claim and the course share, then the keyword score) and returned with their evidence for the person to choose. None is chosen for them: present each candidate and let the person decide. On the agent path (`agent`: the package holds only a document Selfie, through GoldSeam), no AI is called either: the candidates are ranked and returned as on the Selfie interview path, for the person to choose. On the OpenAI path (`openai`: a document Selfie, AcademyOne's own GoldRibbon app), an AI recommender chooses at most one course per claim. Each suggestion is a case to put to the school's prior learning review, never a promise: say may, never will. Nothing is stored: the answer returns the package with the suggestions for the agent to keep.

tools.name: mail_my_bio
tools.description: The bio builder: mail the person, as a Word (.docx) document that Word, Google Docs and Pages open, the resume, CV, profile or portfolio written from their Selfie. resume: one or two pages for an application (a summary, experience, education and training, and skills). cv: the full record (education, work, training, service, projects and life experiences). profile: a short profile to share with an advisor, an employer or online (a headline, an about paragraph and strengths). portfolio: the written portfolio and summary to share with others (a summary in plain words, the statements by grouping with what each came from and its supporting evidence, then the interests and possibilities explored). Write it from show_me_my_selfie's answer and the person's own words, mark proposed statements as proposed, and show it in the chat for them to review and change first. Call this only on the person's own yes, to the address they type in the chat, with their words asking for it as person_consent. The document is the title, then the sections in order; with selfie_coding true it adds a closing Selfie coding section read from the package (each statement not set aside under its KSA grouping, with its KSA Dictionary connection and its affirmation, proposed ones marked proposed); every document closes with the Selfie's distinctions (the person's own words and affirmations; supporting evidence supports, it does not verify; no third-party verification; nothing in it is a qualification or a score). It is sent through the one mail service here: no copy is kept of the document, and the service's mail log records the address, the kind and the document's size, never the document. The first time an address is used, the service emails it a confirmation link first and this answers status waiting_for_confirmation; nothing is mailed to that address until the person opens the link, then call again with the same document. Over a daily limit it answers needs_attention mail_refused with the reason. With no mail setting on the server it answers needs_attention mail_not_configured and sends nothing: give the person the document in the chat.

tools.name: email_me
tools.description: Email the person something they asked for, through the one mail service here, sent from Guided by AcademyOne for KSAWorks. Call it only on the person's own request, to the address they typed in this chat as their own; never a third party's address. kind is one of: resume, bio, progress_link, playlist_ready, invitation (a copy for the person), return_link; each has its own subject, header and footer. payload is the content: text, HTML, a link, or one attached file (a PDF or a Word DOCX, up to 5 MB, as base64). The first time an address is used, the service emails it one confirmation link first and answers status waiting_for_confirmation: nothing else goes to that address until the person opens the link, then call again. An address gets at most 10 emails a day and the service 200; over a limit, or for an unknown kind, an address that is not one, or an empty payload, it answers status refused with the reason. A send that could not go answers status failed with the reason. With no mail setting on the server it answers refused, "Email is not set up on this server.", and sends nothing: give the person what they asked for in the chat. The mail log records the address, the kind, who asked, the outcome and the payload's kind and size, never the payload.
